vendors.name: Eagle 3D Streaming (E3DS)
vendors.linux_build: YES. Linux-packaged Unreal builds are officially supported. Zip the Linux package, then in the Control Panel use Add Application, choose platform type Linux, and give an app name that exactly matches the .sh launch script at the root of the zip. Then create a stream config, open Advanced Options and set Platform = 'Linux UE Build for PS'. Caveats from E3DS's own docs: Linux uploads are NOT launched and stream-tested the way Windows uploads are (the upload only rejects a zip with no Pixel Streaming plugin files). Linux streams start more slowly because Linux machines are not kept warm. Linux VR is unsupported.
vendors.ue_versions: Original Pixel Streaming plugin: UE 5.1 to 5.8. Pixel Streaming 2: UE 5.7 and later only. A UE 5.5 or 5.6 build with PS2 is rejected at upload. Their two compatibility pages disagree on whether browser-to-Unreal messaging works with PS2; one says it is not supported. UE 5.9 is NOT listed (it is still a preview engine, see notes). The Linux cross-compile toolchain must match the engine version. We package natively on Linux, so this does not apply to us.
vendors.embed: Share link or iframe. Their embed guide uses an iframe with id 'iframe_1' and a script that focuses it on load so WASD reaches the game. The parent page can send keyboard events through postMessage JSON. Fullscreen needs the iframe's allow permission. Unreal-side settings cover locked vs hovering mouse modes and not capturing the mouse at launch, and a browser-drawn cursor is recommended. An optional E3DS Features plugin and SDK add custom UI and messaging, but the Features plugin is built only for the original PS plugin.
vendors.gamepad: Yes, according to the vendor. PlayStation, Xbox and standard gamepads work through the browser Gamepad API (Chrome or Edge recommended) with no platform setup, as long as the project keeps Unreal's default controller input mappings.
vendors.audio: Standard Pixel Streaming WebRTC audio. No E3DS-specific audio limits were found in the docs. Browsers still need a click before audio plays.
vendors.pricing: Trial: free, 60 lifetime minutes, 1 concurrent stream, no credit card. Core: $29/month or $290/year, 300 minutes/month (unused minutes expire), 10 concurrent streams. Extra minutes are $0.10/min, bought in steps of 100. You are never billed automatically: streaming stops when minutes run out. Enterprise: custom price at about $0.10/min, up to 1,000 concurrent streams, global regions. Storage figures conflict (5 or 10 GB on Trial, 10 or 250 GB on Core). About $6 per player-hour beyond the included minutes.
vendors.regions: Trial and Core: US (Texas, according to the pricing page) and EU, with viewers sent to the nearer one automatically. Enterprise: global, also deployable on AWS, GCP and Azure. E3DS's own datacentre GPUs are RTX 4080 and RTX 5070. Cloud-provider machines are typically T4 or A10. No latency figures in milliseconds are published.
vendors.notes: Concurrency: one CCU per active player in Dedicated mode. Players beyond the CCU limit wait in a queue until someone leaves. Session controls include Max Session Time, inactivity logout and link expiration (exact defaults not found). Load time: about 20-30 s for a first start, 10-20 s for frequently streamed apps, under 10 s for pre-allocated apps (Enterprise), and slower on Linux. Video must appear within 3 minutes or the start counts as failed. Resource guidance: stay within about 20 GB RAM and 4-6 GB VRAM at 50-70% GPU use, or risk 'Out of Video Memory' crashes. This is the main technical risk for a Lumen + Nanite + hardware-RT shooter and must be measured. No public content or acceptable-use rules for a violent game were found; the legal page did not show them. Upload automation is available through an editor plugin and a Node/CI package. Research limit: this session could not open docs.eagle3dstreaming.com directly, so these facts come from search-indexed copies of the cited pages. Re-check them on the live pages.

vendors.name: Amazon GameLift Streams (AWS)
vendors.linux_build: YES, natively. The Ubuntu 22.04 LTS runtime runs Linux builds. The executable must be a valid Linux binary or a shebang script, must not need root, and renders through X11. It is generic application streaming over WebRTC, so no Pixel Streaming plugin is needed. Windows and Proton runtimes also exist.
vendors.ue_versions: Windows runtime: documented as UE 4.27 and UE 5 up to 5.6 (older copies say 5.5). The docs give no UE version ceiling for native Linux builds. Because the service runs any Linux binary, the engine version should not matter, but 5.9 is untested.
vendors.embed: No ready-made embed link for a public site. You integrate the AWS Web SDK into your own page and run a small backend that calls StartStreamSession. CreateStreamUrl can produce browser links without client integration, but each URL has a usage limit (default 1, maximum 50), so a public site still needs a backend to issue them. Pointer lock is built in (autoPointerLock: true, false or 'fullscreen', no effect on Safari or iOS). Keyboard and mouse supported. Chrome and Edge recommended.
vendors.gamepad: Web SDK supports W3C gamepads. On the Ubuntu runtime, gamepad support only works for apps that use SDL. Unreal's Linux input layer is SDL-based (our inference, to be tested).
vendors.audio: Yes. The SDK needs separate video and audio elements, and audio must be unlocked by a user gesture. No microphone on the Ubuntu runtime.
vendors.pricing: Billed per second for allocated stream capacity, whether or not anyone is playing, plus storage per GB-month. No AWS Free Tier. Examples: gen4n_high (T4, 2 players per GPU) at about $0.50/capacity-hour in Oregon and about $0.66 in Frankfurt. gen6n_small at $0.16/hour in Ohio (12 sessions per GPU, far too small for this game). gen6n_ultra (Windows) at about $1.82/hour in Oregon. Minimum capacity can be 0, and autoscaling was added in Dec 2025.
vendors.regions: 12 AWS regions: us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, sa-east-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-north-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-northeast-2, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-2. Stream classes vary by location. GPUs: T4 (gen4n), A10G (gen5n_ultra), L4 (gen6).
vendors.notes: Sessions last at most 24 h (default 12 h) and end after 60 minutes with no input. The GPU quota defaults to 0 and needs a service-quota increase. One per-application spec lists 2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM and 6 GB VRAM, which is tight for Lumen with hardware ray tracing. This is the strongest fallback: Linux-native and engine-version-agnostic. But it is not a 'give me an embed link' service: the owner needs an AWS account and someone must build and host the session backend, which goes against the owner's managed-service choice.

vendors.name: Vagon Streams
vendors.linux_build: PARTLY. Vagon's Unreal Pixel Streaming mode is Windows-only (its docs say Pixel Streaming and Unity Render Streaming support only Windows builds). Its own 'Application Streaming' mode lists Windows and Linux apps 'with the same feature capabilities', and the upload flow starts with an Application Type step (Windows or Linux). But the same guide still says the main executable must be a .exe at the zip root, so whether a Linux Unreal build uploads cleanly is unconfirmed.
vendors.ue_versions: No UE version list was found. The Pixel Streaming upload checks the build's UE version and plugin. Application Streaming runs the binary as an app.
vendors.embed: Stream link or iframe, controlled by the Vagon JS SDK: startStream (must run from a click), focusIframe, enable/disableGameMode, onPointerLockChange, setVideoVolume, keepAlive and shutdown. The iframe needs the right permissions. Custom stream URL on the Pro plan.
vendors.gamepad: Controller support is claimed, including an on-screen controller mapped to PS4 stick inputs. Physical gamepad support in the browser is not clearly documented.
vendors.audio: Yes. Sound and microphone modes are set per stream (off, on at start, user-activated).
vendors.pricing: Per minute: Windows from $0.025/min (T4 Starter), $0.035 (T4 Pro), about $0.036-0.047 (A10G or L4). Linux from $0.018/min (about $1.08/hour). A separate idle fee of $0.67/day per deployment location keeps the app ready. Basic plan free (25 apps, 20+ regions). Pro $99.99/month (50 apps, custom URL).
vendors.regions: 20+ regions, including Virginia, Oregon, São Paulo, Dublin, Frankfurt, Stockholm, Bahrain, Dubai, Tokyo, Singapore and Sydney. GPUs: T4, A10G, L4.
vendors.notes: Concurrency limits conflict: the pricing page says 25 concurrent sessions per region on the free plan and 50 on Pro, while marketing says 'unlimited'. The API has a 'waiting in queue' state, while a blog post says there is no queue. Session settings include maximum_session_duration, idle_duration and auto_turn_off_duration. The terms ban illegal use, IP infringement and malware. No bandwidth cap or specific rule on violent content was found. The GPUs are weaker than E3DS's RTX 4080/5070. A possible second choice if Linux Application Streaming is confirmed. Research limit: docs.vagon.io could not be opened directly from this session, so facts come from search-indexed copies.

vendors.name: Arcware Cloud (CloudRT)
vendors.linux_build: NO, not documented. The docs describe uploading a zipped package that is virus-scanned and test-launched. All engine settings they give are Windows ones (DirectX 11/12, with DX12 recommended under Project Settings > Platforms > Windows), and no page mentions Linux packages. Treat it as Windows-only unless Arcware confirms otherwise.
vendors.ue_versions: UE 5.1 to 5.8 active and tested (5.8 is the latest). 4.27 and 5.0.3 are deprecated. 5.9 is not listed. Uploads with both Pixel Streaming and Pixel Streaming 2 enabled are blocked.
vendors.embed: Share link (share.arcware.cloud, revocable Share ID) or the Arcware Pixel Streaming WebSDK (npm @arcware-cloud/pixelstreaming-websdk). The docs strongly advise using the WebSDK rather than an iframe. Mouse Lock is a project setting, its direction is described inconsistently, and it is marked experimental.
vendors.gamepad: Yes. The WebSDK has a gamepad input toggle, alongside keyboard, mouse and touch.
vendors.audio: Yes. Audio mute button and optional microphone (needs a user gesture).
vendors.pricing: Trial: 15 days, 60 minutes, 2 concurrent streams. Lite: €10/month plus €0.15/min. Core: €89/month plus ≤€0.10/min, 3-10 concurrent streams per project. Custom: ≤€0.08/min. Prepaid minute bundles in the marketplace. Expert support €150/hour. The indexed pricing page is old, so re-check it.
vendors.regions: One location per project: Munich (EU) or Los Angeles (US). Multi-region was promised for an Enterprise plan. Claimed latency: about 20 ms in the DACH region, 50 ms in Europe, 80 ms on the US East Coast, 150 ms on the US West Coast. NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, model not stated.
vendors.notes: Built-in queue in the WebSDK. Settings for maximum instance run-time, AFK timeout and reconnection grace time. Polished option for Windows builds, but our Linux build is ruled out.

vendors.name: PureWeb Reality
vendors.linux_build: NO. The current packaging guide says 'package your game for Windows only'. Upload goes through console.pureweb.io or the pw CLI with --exe Game/Game.exe. After the first upload, PureWeb support must deploy the model manually.
vendors.ue_versions: The supported-versions page lists 5.4.x, 5.3.x and 4.27.x. A 'Prepare your Unreal 5.5 package' guide also exists. Nothing for 5.6 or later.
vendors.embed: PureWeb client SDK and plugin. Not researched further because Windows builds are required.
vendors.pricing: Core (Pixel and Render Streaming) from $750/month. VR Core from $1,000/month. Overage billed per session, rounded up to the next full minute.
vendors.notes: Owned by Banyan Software since Jan 2024 and still operating. Aimed at enterprise. Ruled out: Windows-only, older UE versions and a high minimum price.

vendors.name: Epic Games (own options)
vendors.linux_build: Not applicable: Epic runs no managed hosting service. It publishes the self-hosted Pixel Streaming Infrastructure (signalling server, SFU, front-end libraries) on GitHub, which supports Linux, and the Matchmaker is deprecated from UE 5.5. This is what we use on the box for the demo route, but the box cannot serve the public.
vendors.ue_versions: One branch of the infrastructure per engine version. UE 5.9 is in Preview: Epic's 5.9 release notes are dated 9 Nov 2026, and press reports say UE 5.8 is the latest full release.
vendors.embed: Self-hosted front end (web component or iframe), built by us.
vendors.gamepad: Pixel Streaming front end supports browser gamepads (self-hosted).
vendors.pricing: Free software. You pay for your own GPUs.
vendors.notes: Not a managed option. Listed only so the owner knows Epic does not offer one.

vendors.name: Make Live (TensorWorks) and Scalable Pixel Streaming
vendors.linux_build: Make Live was Linux-only by design ('build your project for Linux, and upload'). Scalable Pixel Streaming (SPS) runs Windows or Linux containers on Kubernetes (CoreWeave, AWS EKS).
vendors.ue_versions: Not documented in what we could find.
vendors.embed: Not documented in what we could find.
vendors.pricing: Make Live pricing page: T4 or RTX 3060 Ti $0.026/min, RTX 3080 $0.032/min, RTX 3090 $0.048/min (Linux). SPS: no public price; it is deployed into your own cloud account.
vendors.notes: Not recommended. Forum posts report Make Live is 'not working anymore', and SPS is a self-deploy framework, not a managed embed-link service. Listed for completeness.

research.recommendation:
Use Eagle 3D Streaming (E3DS). Keep Amazon GameLift Streams as the fallback.

Why E3DS:
1. It is the only managed Pixel Streaming host whose current docs explicitly accept a Linux-packaged Unreal build. It has a documented upload path (zip with the .sh at the root, platform Linux, config platform 'Linux UE Build for PS'), so no Windows machine is needed. Arcware and PureWeb document Windows-only packages, and Vagon's Pixel Streaming mode is Windows-only.
2. It matches the owner's chosen model: the owner creates the account and uploads, and E3DS hosts, scales, queues extra players and hands out a share link or iframe.
3. Gamepads work through the browser with Unreal's default mappings. Keyboard focus, fullscreen and pointer modes for an iframe are documented.
4. Its datacentre GPUs (RTX 4080 / RTX 5070) suit Lumen, Nanite and hardware ray tracing better than the T4, A10G or L4 used by Vagon and AWS.
5. Lowest start cost: a free 60-minute trial with no card, then Core at $29/month (300 minutes, 10 concurrent players, US and EU), extra minutes at $0.10 (about $6 per player-hour), and no automatic overage billing.

Risks the owner must accept:
- Our engine is UE 5.9.0 Preview 2. E3DS lists Pixel Streaming 2 support only for 5.7 and 5.8, and no vendor lists 5.9. Linux uploads are not stream-tested by E3DS, so the first real test is opening the link.
- E3DS asks apps to stay within about 4-6 GB VRAM and 20 GB RAM, so we must measure and cap the game's VRAM for the cloud.
- Linux streams start more slowly (machines are not kept warm), and one of their pages says browser-to-Unreal messaging is not supported with Pixel Streaming 2.
- No public content policy was found. The owner should read E3DS's Terms before publishing a violent shooter.

If E3DS rejects the 5.9 build, or VRAM or start times fail, fall back to Amazon GameLift Streams on its Ubuntu 22.04 runtime. It runs any Linux binary (no Pixel Streaming plugin, so the engine version should not matter) and has built-in pointer lock, gamepads (SDL) and 12 regions. It costs about $0.50 per capacity-hour on gen4n_high or more on A10G, billed while capacity is allocated. It needs an AWS account, a GPU quota increase and a small session backend on the IPX site.

Vagon's Linux Application Streaming ($0.018/min plus $0.67/day per region) is a third option, once Vagon confirms that a non-.exe Linux Unreal build uploads.

Research limit: WebFetch could not reach docs.eagle3dstreaming.com or docs.vagon.io from this session. Every fact comes from search-engine copies of the cited pages, so re-check prices and limits on the live pages before paying.
steps: US: Make the cloud build. Package a Linux Shipping build on the box with exactly one streaming plugin enabled: Pixel Streaming 2. Do not enable both plugins, as hosts block or reject that. Keep Unreal's default gamepad mappings and add our own Enhanced Input gamepad bindings. Hide the in-video cursor and use the browser cursor for menus. Start audio on the first click. Make sure the launch script at the package root has the name we will give the app (for example MurderInc.sh). Zip the package so that .sh sits at the zip root.

US: Check the build on the box first, with Epic's Pixel Streaming Infrastructure, as the demo route in docs/DEMO.md does. On a 1080p stream, measure VRAM, RAM, GPU use and input-to-picture latency. Target E3DS's guidance: VRAM about 4-6 GB, RAM under 20 GB, GPU 50-70%. Add a 'cloud' scalability profile (lower Lumen and ray-tracing settings, capped resolution and frame rate) if needed. Write the figures in docs/unreal.

US: Write a short hand-off sheet for the owner. It covers the zip, the exact app name (= .sh name), the Unreal version and plugin, and the iframe snippet with allow="autoplay; fullscreen; gamepad; pointer-lock; clipboard-read; clipboard-write" and id="iframe_1". It also covers the focus-on-load script and a click-to-start overlay for the Game OS page.

OWNER: Read E3DS's current Terms of Service and acceptable-use rules (for a public, violent shooter) and the current pricing page. Then create an Eagle 3D Streaming account on the free Trial (60 minutes, no credit card). Do not share our build or account details anywhere else.

OWNER: In the E3DS Control Panel, click Add Application, select our zip, choose platform type Linux, and enter the app name exactly as the .sh file is named. Wait for every upload phase to finish, plus a few minutes for the build to sync to servers.

OWNER: Create a stream config for the app. Under Advanced Options set Platform = 'Linux UE Build for PS' (a config left on Windows waits forever). Pick the region (US, EU or automatic), resolution, mouse or pointer mode, inactivity logout, link expiration and Max Session Time.

OWNER + US: Open the share link in Chrome and Edge, and test it ourselves, because E3DS does not stream-test Linux uploads. Check start time, click-to-start, pointer lock and mouse look, keyboard, an Xbox or PlayStation pad, audio, a lost-connection reconnect, and the queue with 2 players on the Trial's 1 concurrent stream. Record latency and minutes used. If the upload is rejected for UE 5.9 or the stream never appears, stop and go to the fallback step.
OWNER: Put the E3DS iframe (our snippet) on the IPX.exchange Game OS page with the fullscreen permission and the focus script. Then test it again from the real page.

OWNER: Before opening to the public, subscribe to Core ($29/month or $290/year: 300 minutes, 10 concurrent players, US and EU). Buy extra minutes in steps of 100 ($0.10/min) as needed, knowing streaming stops when minutes run out. Players beyond 10 wait in E3DS's queue. Go to Enterprise (about $0.10/min, up to 1,000 concurrent, global regions, faster pre-allocated starts) only if traffic justifies it.

US: After launch, track cost per player-hour and peak concurrency from the E3DS dashboard and record them in DECISIONS.md or PROGRESS.md. Re-package and upload (manually, or with E3DS's Node/CI upload package) for each update. Move the project to the final UE 5.9 release when Epic ships it.

FALLBACK (only if E3DS fails on 5.9, VRAM or start time): the owner opens an AWS account, requests a GameLift Streams GPU quota for gen4n_high or gen5n_ultra in us-east-2 or eu-central-1, and uploads the same Linux build to S3 as an Ubuntu 22.04 application. We write a small session backend (StartStreamSession, or CreateStreamUrl) plus the AWS Web SDK player for the Game OS page, with autoPointerLock and gamepads. Set minimum capacity to 0 or 1 to control idle cost.
research.windows_needed: false. Eagle 3D Streaming documents a full Linux upload path, so no Windows packaging machine is needed: zip with the .sh at the root, Control Panel platform 'Linux', config platform 'Linux UE Build for PS'. Two fallbacks also run Linux builds: Amazon GameLift Streams on its Ubuntu 22.04 runtime, and possibly Vagon Application Streaming. A Windows package would only be needed to use Arcware Cloud, PureWeb or Vagon's Pixel Streaming mode, which all document Windows builds only. If that ever becomes necessary, the cheapest realistic route is an hourly Windows cloud VM with enough disk (about 200+ GB) and CPU, used only while packaging and then shut down. On it we would install the same UE 5.9 build, copy the project, run BuildCookRun for Win64, and download the zip. Packaging does not need a strong GPU. Before relying on Eagle, there is a separate engine-version risk: UE 5.9 is still Preview 2 and no host lists 5.9. If E3DS rejects the build, the fix is the GameLift Streams fallback (engine-agnostic), not a Windows machine.

corrections: E3DS resource guidance ("stay within about 20 GB RAM and 4-6 GB VRAM at 50-70% GPU"): no search-indexed copy of E3DS's system-requirements or hardware pages gives these figures. What they do say is that a standard server has 32 GB RAM, 8 GB or 16 GB of GPU VRAM, an i7/R7-class CPU and an RTX 4080 or RTX 5070. An older Confluence page says RTX 3070/4080. They also say an app that uses more than the server has may crash, and Out of Video Memory is the most common failure. Treat 4-6 GB / 20 GB as unverified, and use 8 GB VRAM (the worst case) as the cloud budget until E3DS confirms. Sources: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/hardware-and-software-specifications , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/system-requirements , https://eagle3dstreaming.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/docs/pages/13762563/Hardware+and+Software+Specifications

E3DS Linux upload check ("the upload only rejects a zip with no Pixel Streaming plugin files"): E3DS's Current Limitations page says the platform "does not perform stream testing to verify if the Pixel Streaming plugin is enabled in your build". Its workaround is that you confirm this yourself before uploading. Nothing found says the upload rejects a zip that lacks the plugin. Source: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/current-limitations-and-solutions

E3DS config location ("open Advanced Options and set Platform = 'Linux UE Build for PS'"): the indexed E3DS config page says to choose 'Linux UE Build for PS' from the Platform option in the Development tab, then save. The setting name is right but the tab is named differently. Step 6 of the plan should say Development tab, or 'wherever Platform appears'. Source: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/create-a-config-for-linux-build-streaming

E3DS billing ("You are never billed automatically"): this is true for Core and Trial, where streaming pauses when minutes run out and resumes on purchase or renewal. It is not true of every E3DS plan. Prepaid-minute plans have an auto-recharge setting, and the pay-per-minute 'streaming cap' is post-paid, billed monthly, starting at 100 min for $10, with a 'Remove Capping' button. The owner should stay on Core or Prepaid with auto-recharge off. Sources: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/core-plan-usage-billing , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/prepaid-minute-plan-usage-billing , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/minutes-streamed-limit

E3DS region ('US (Texas, according to the pricing page)'): the Texas datacentre is named on an older Confluence page, not the pricing page. Current docs say only that Trial and Core deploy in the USA and Europe, with automatic routing to the next-closest region. Sources: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/datacenter-routing , https://eagle3dstreaming.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/docs/pages/564854786

E3DS Linux packaging: E3DS's Linux guide and blog describe building the Linux package on Windows with Unreal's cross-compile toolchain, which must match the UE version. No E3DS page found explicitly covers a package built natively on Linux. The output should be equivalent, but saying 'this does not apply to us' is an inference, not a documented fact. Sources: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/create-a-linux-build , https://www.eagle3dstreaming.com/blog/package-linux-build-on-windows-os-for-linux-pixel-streaming

E3DS PS2 on Linux: the plan tells us to ship Linux with Pixel Streaming 2 only. E3DS's PS2 compatibility page documents PS2 on UE 5.7+ for standard playback, says communication is not supported, and says nothing about platform. No E3DS page confirms PS2 on Linux builds. A third-party forum thread reports colour-tint problems with UE 5.5 PS2 on Linux. The combination 'Linux + PS2 + UE 5.9' is undocumented on all three counts, not only on the engine version. Sources: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/pixel-streaming-plugin-2-compatibility , https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/unreal-engine-5-5-on-linux-pixel-streaming-rendering-issues-red-blue-green-tint/2388393

GameLift Streams gamepad on Ubuntu 22.04 ('gamepad support only works for apps that use SDL'): AWS's own pages contradict each other. The FAQ and the Configuration options page say gamepad support is NOT available on the Ubuntu 22.04 LTS runtime, and the Supported browsers and input page says the same ('except for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS'). The compatible-devices page and the troubleshooting guide say gamepads work only for SDL apps, and suggest Proton or Windows otherwise. The analyst reported only the favourable wording, so treat gamepads on the Linux fallback as unconfirmed. Sources: https://aws.amazon.com/gamelift/streams/faqs/ , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/configuration-options.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/sdk-browsers-input.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/compatible-devices-browsers.html

GameLift Streams resources ('One per-application spec lists 2 vCPU, 8 GB RAM and 6 GB VRAM, which is tight'; 'gen6n_ultra (Windows)'): per the configuration-options page and its translations, gen4n_high is a T4 at 2 sessions per GPU with about 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM and 8 GB VRAM per session. The Linux classes gen5n_ultra (A10G) and gen6n_ultra (L4) each give 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM and 24 GB VRAM to a single session. gen6n_ultra is a Linux class; the Windows variant is gen6n_ultra_win2022. Some translated or older copies list 16 GB VRAM for gen5n_ultra. So AWS can offer more VRAM per player than E3DS's 8/16 GB servers. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/configuration-options.html

Recommendation reason 4 ('E3DS RTX 4080/5070 suit Lumen/Nanite/HW-RT better than T4, A10G or L4 used by Vagon and AWS'): this is not supported as stated. The RTX 4080 has 16 GB of VRAM and the RTX 5070 12 GB, and E3DS lists 8 or 16 GB per server. AWS gen5n_ultra and gen6n_ultra give one session a full 24 GB A10G or L4. RTX 40/50 cards are faster at ray tracing, but for the stated main risk (VRAM / Out of Video Memory), the AWS ultra classes have more headroom. Sources: https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/hardware-and-software-specifications , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/configuration-options.html

GameLift Streams CreateStreamUrl ('usage limit default 1, maximum 50'): AWS docs confirm minimum 1 and default 1, a status of LIMIT_REACHED when the limit is used up, and a separate UrlExpiresAfterMinutes. No source found gives the maximum of 50. AWS announced stream-URL sharing in Aug 2026. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/apireference/API_CreateStreamUrl.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/stream-urls.html , https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/amazon-gamelift-streams/

Vagon plans ('Basic plan free (25 apps, 20+ regions). Pro $99.99/month (50 apps, custom URL)'): the sources conflict. Vagon's Streams page lists $99.99/mo next to 'up to 5 users' on what may be a stale page. A third-party aggregator (xpay, May 2026) calls Basic $99.99/mo and says paid plans go up to $249/mo. No source found confirms a free Basic plan or the 25- and 50-app counts. Sources: https://vagon.io/streams , https://vagon.io/streams/pricing , https://www.xpay.sh/saas-pricing/vagon-streams/

Vagon idle fee ('a separate idle fee of $0.67/day per deployment location'): the pricing page describes $0.67/day per selected location as the calculator's assumption for 'application maintenance'. It also says the calculator excludes Advanced Setup reserved or idle machine costs. Calling it an 'idle fee' and treating it as the only idle cost is not supported. Source: https://vagon.io/streams/pricing

PureWeb ('The current packaging guide says package your game for Windows only'): the indexed 'package your project for Windows only' wording is in PureWeb's Unreal 5.2 packaging guide. No 5.4-specific guide was found. The Windows-only conclusion still stands, since no Linux path is documented anywhere. Also, PureWeb's Core plan GPUs are T4 and RTX 5000. Sources: https://developer.pureweb.io/prepare-your-unreal-5-project/amp/ , https://www.pureweb.com/pricing/
verified: E3DS supports Linux-packaged Unreal builds: there is a Linux Pixel Streaming guide with the same build, upload and stream flow as Windows, plus a Linux-specific naming rule at upload and a config Platform option named 'Linux UE Build for PS'. Linux builds load more slowly (no dedicated or warm Linux infrastructure, due to low demand). Linux VR is untested. https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/linux-pixel-streaming , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/create-a-config-for-linux-build-streaming , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/why-load-time-is-high , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/getting-started-with-linux-pixel-streaming

E3DS PS2: supported on UE 5.7 and later (5.8 stable) for standard playback. UE 5.5 and 5.6 with PS2 are not supported. Browser-to-Unreal and Unreal-to-browser messaging is not supported with PS2, and E3DS recommends PS1 for that. An older E3DS page says PS2 is not supported at all, so the two pages conflict as reported. UE 5.9 is not listed. https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/pixel-streaming-plugin-2-compatibility , https://eagle3dstreaming.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/docs/pages/865075202/Pixel+Streaming+Plugin+2+Compatibility

E3DS pricing: Core $29/month, 300 minutes/month, $0.10/min after that, 10 concurrent streams, 2 months free on annual billing ($290/yr consistent). Minutes do not roll over. Trial: 60 free lifetime minutes, no card, 5 GB, and it pauses when used up. Enterprise is listed at $0.10/min (an older 'upcoming pricing' page says $0.08). Storage conflict confirmed: 10 GB in the calculator versus 'up to 250 GB' purchasable. Trial and Core cover the USA and Europe with automatic nearest-region routing. Enterprise has global regions. https://eagle3dstreaming.com/pricing , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/core-plan-usage-billing , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/trial-plan-usage , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/datacenter-routing , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/faq-frequently-asked-questions

E3DS gamepads: PlayStation, Xbox and standard gamepads work with no platform setup, provided the project's Unreal input mappings exist (Epic templates ship with them). Browsers report a controller only to the focused page, so an iframe on our site needs one click on the stream first. https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/game-controller-support

E3DS embed: an iframe embed guide exists, with a focus-on-load script so WASD reaches the game, keyboard input forwarding from the parent page, and hover/locked mouse switching inside the iframe. The exact id 'iframe_1' and a gamepad 'allow' token were NOT confirmed. The guide's sample allow attribute shows xr-spatial-tracking, camera and microphone. https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/embed-e3ds-app-with-your-html-webpage , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/send-keyboard-input-to-a-ue-app-from-iframe , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/switch-between-hover-and-locked-mouse-in-iframe

E3DS session controls exist: Max Session Time, logout after inactivity and link expiration. https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/max-session-time , https://docs.eagle3dstreaming.com/wiki/logout-automatically-after-inactivity , https://eagle3dstreaming.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/docs/pages/337739906

GameLift Streams: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS is a Linux runtime, and Proton runtimes exist (Proton 10 added Apr 2026). UE support up to 5.6 is documented only for the Windows runtime, and no UE ceiling is documented for Ubuntu. AWS's own blog packages UE 5.6 with Proton on the Linux runtime. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/configuration-options.html , https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/gametech/run-unreal-engine-5-6-with-proton-on-amazon-gamelift-streams-linux-runtime/ , https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/04/amazon-gamelift-streams-proton-10-runtime/

GameLift Streams pricing: billed per second for allocated capacity whether idle or streaming. gen4n_high about $0.4982/capacity-hour in us-west-2 and about $0.6571 in eu-central-1. gen6n_small $0.16/hour in us-east-2. Gen6 classes and enhanced autoscaling launched Dec 2025. https://aws.amazon.com/gamelift/streams/pricing/ , https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/aws-gameliftstream-gen6-enhanced-autoscaling/

GameLift Streams Web SDK: autoPointerLock accepts true, false or 'fullscreen' (the default) and has no effect on Safari or iOS. StartStreamSession defaults to a 12 h session length and a 120 s connection timeout. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/sdk-mouse-movement.html , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/apireference/API_StartStreamSession.html

GameLift Streams regions: six new regions were added in Jan 2026 with all stream classes, and remote locations are supported. The exact 12-region list was NOT verified. https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/01/glstreams-new-regions , https://docs.aws.amazon.com/gameliftstreams/latest/developerguide/regions-quotas-rande.html

Vagon: Unreal Pixel Streaming is only for Windows-built Unreal experiences. Application Streaming lists both Windows and Linux 'with the same feature capabilities', and the upload flow has an Application Type step. The same guide still says the main executable must be a .exe at the zip root, so whether a Linux build uploads cleanly is unresolved, as reported. Linux from $0.018/min and Windows from $0.025/min are confirmed. GPU per-minute rates: T4 Starter $0.025, T4 Pro $0.035, A10G $0.036/$0.046, L4 $0.036/$0.047. 20+ regions. https://docs.vagon.io/streams/unreal-engine-pixel-streaming , https://docs.vagon.io/streams/guides/how-to-start-streaming , https://vagon.io/streams/features/application-streaming , https://vagon.io/streams/pricing

Arcware: UE 5.1 to 5.8 active (5.8 latest), 4.27 and 5.0.3 deprecated, no 5.9. Uploads are zipped, virus-scanned and checked for the PS plugin and a clean startup. Only DirectX 11/12 settings are documented and no Linux path was found, consistent with 'treat as Windows-only'. Pricing (page about 1000 days old): 15-day trial with no card. Lite €10/month plus €0.15/min, 1 project, 2 concurrent streams. Core €89/month plus ≤€0.10/min, 3-10 concurrent per project. https://docs.arcware.cloud/unreal-engine-setup/unreal-engine-version-support , https://docs.arcware.cloud/arcware-cloud-platform/getting-started-with-arcware-cloud/creating-and-managing-your-projects/uploading-and-releasing-packages , https://docs.arcware.cloud/unreal-engine-setup/set-up-pixel-streaming-in-your-own-project/core-settings/directx-version , https://www.arcware.com/pricing

PureWeb: supported versions are 5.4.x, 5.3.x (platform only) and 4.27.x, with 5.2 deprecated. Core starts at $750/month and VR Core at $1,000/month. Overage is billed per session, rounded up to the next full minute. https://developer.pureweb.io/supported-unreal-versions/ , https://developer.pureweb.io/release-notes/ , https://www.pureweb.com/pricing/ , https://www.pureweb.com/terms-of-service/

Epic: the UE 5.9 release notes are dated 9 Nov 2026 and the forum thread is titled '[Preview 2] Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview'. Epic calls Preview builds unstable until the final release, so 5.8 is the latest full release. Not in the report: the 5.9 Preview also brings back running projects in the browser through WebAssembly/WebGPU, which Epic calls a prototype. https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-5-9-release-notes , https://forums.unrealengine.com/t/2852840 , https://digitalproduction.com/2026/11/16/unreal-engine-5-9-preview-agents-canvas-and-a-browser-sized-ambition/
verify.recommendation_holds:
Partly true. Eagle 3D Streaming should stay first choice, but some of the reasons and risks need rewriting.

What still holds:
- E3DS is still the only managed Pixel Streaming host found whose own docs accept a Linux Unreal package and return a share link or iframe.
- Arcware, PureWeb and Vagon's Pixel Streaming mode still document Windows builds only.
- The E3DS points that drive the choice check out: the Core price ($29, 300 min, 10 concurrent streams, $0.10/min), the free 60-minute trial with no card, the pause when minutes run out on Core, US and EU regions, gamepads with no setup, and the iframe focus guidance.
- So windows_needed=false still stands.

What must change before the owner acts on it:
1. The GPU argument (reason 4) is not supported. E3DS servers have 8 or 16 GB of VRAM. AWS gen5n_ultra and gen6n_ultra give one player 24 GB on Linux. The '4-6 GB VRAM / 20 GB RAM' target was not found anywhere, so budget the cloud build against 8 GB.
2. The plan's main path, 'Linux + Pixel Streaming 2 + UE 5.9', is undocumented on all three counts. E3DS documents PS2 only for UE 5.7+ and never for Linux. E3DS also does not check that the plugin is enabled. The first upload is therefore the real test, and that test should come before anything is paid for.
3. The AWS fallback's gamepad claim is contradicted by AWS's own FAQ and configuration page, which say gamepads are not available on Ubuntu 22.04; other pages say SDL apps only. That fallback may need the Proton or Windows runtime if gamepads matter.
4. Smaller fixes: the E3DS Platform setting is in the Development tab; the Texas location comes from an older page; and the 'never billed automatically' promise holds only on Core or Trial, not on prepaid plans with auto-recharge or the post-paid streaming cap.
5. The Vagon plan names and prices conflict between sources.

Limits of this check: WebFetch could not reach eagle3dstreaming.com, docs.eagle3dstreaming.com, aws.amazon.com or docs.aws.amazon.com from this session (DNS blocked). Everything above comes from search-engine copies of the cited pages, so re-check prices and limits on the live pages before paying.
